title: Understanding PCA Decomposition
text: In PCA, the matrix $X$ is decomposed into three matrices: $U$, $\Sigma$, and $V**{T}$. The matrix $V**{T}$ is the transpose of the matrix $V$, which contains the principal components.

title: Dimensions of $V**{T}$
text: The dimensions of $V**{T}$ are determined by the number of features (columns) in the original matrix $X$.

title: Counting Features in $X$
text: How many columns does the matrix $X$ have?

title: Conclusion on $c$
text: Since $V**{T}$ is the transpose of $V$, its dimensions are determined by the number of features in $X$. Therefore, $c$ is equal to the number of columns in $X$.
